title: Decode: low-latency dense GEMM family (BF16 + MXFP8)
shape: NVFP4 checkpoint, D3-32 r24 1-node DP-rank slice (24-layer view k31-nvfp4-view-L24, u132k, k=3): R = 384 gathered rows (attention projections), n = 96 shard rows (MoE dense GEMMs) per GPU; per decode step, exposed time
basis: MEASURED in-step (NVFP4 decode baseline, INFRA measured/20261118-1900-nvfp4-decode.json, run rhea runs/INFRA/step_d/trial-9ccf8ab-nv-r8r16r24-prof, overlay trial-9ccf8ab-1 = int b31121cf56 + d-moe). Family = fam.py 'BF16 dense GEMMs' groups (KDA in/o_proj, DSA qkv_a/g/o/w_uv, router+latent_down, latent_up, shared gate_up/down, dense layer). achievable = nvfp4_modelopt model_rows_L24 for the same groups. r8 / r16 rows: 1.201 / 1.311 exposed vs 0.753 / 0.778 achievable.
gap_analysis: Per precision at r24 (exposed vs achievable, us per L24 step): MXFP8 (KDA in/o_proj, shared gate_up/down, quant kernels counted elsewhere) 746 vs 411; BF16 (DSA qkv_a/g/o/w_uv, router+latent_down, latent_up, dense layer) 835 vs 410. Every op in-step is a cuBLAS nvjet kernel (MXFP8: nvjet qqtst Avec32UE8M0). Per call (busy) vs model: KDA in_proj 17.8 vs 7.6 us (92 MB -> 5.2 TB/s), KDA o_proj 7.3 vs 2.1, router+latent_down 3 kernels 20 vs 4.9 (router on main and latent down on aux stream), latent_up 7.4 vs 3.8, DSA qkv_a 15.9 vs 3.4, g_proj 27.6 vs 4.6 (busy, half exposed), DSA o_proj 9.6 vs 4.6, shared down 14.0 vs 3.5 (side stream beside MegaMoE). Root cause: generic library tiles stream weights at 3-7 TB/s (too few bytes in flight per SM, many CTAs per weight byte, separate split-K reduce kernels, no weight prefetch across kernel boundaries); the model streams at 13.9 TB/s striped. MEASURED (stream_gemm prototype stamps, runs/D-GEMM/sg q4-q7): for a dependent GEMM the per-call time is post-dependency latency, not HBM: after griddepcontrol.wait each SM still runs its whole chunk's MMAs (x lands only then) and the ring rounds (~3-4.4 us), then a split-K reduce (~2-5 us through L2 round trips), then the grid-end flush (~2.5 us). Even with every weight byte pre-streamed during the predecessor, latent_down n32 is >= 9.5 us vs the bandwidth-only model 3.7 us.
inefficiencies: cuBLAS nvjet tiles stream weights at 3-7 TB/s in-step [gap.json]
post-dependency path per GEMM (x load + MMA issue over the whole per-SM chunk + split reduce + grid end) ~6-11 us regardless of weight prefetch [stream_gemm stamps q4-q7]
split-K reduce through L2 costs ~4 round trips (~1 us each under load) [stamps: part_stored -> cnt_passed -> done]
MXFP8 activation quant as separate kernels [bench1]
x replicated per 128-row weight tile (R/128 of the weight bytes into each SM) [design analysis]
rubin_features: tcgen05 MMA swap-AB (weights M128, tokens N), TMEM accumulators, 2 segments per CTA
TMA 128B-swizzled boxes, L2 evict_first on streamed weights
1 CTA per SM, whole shared memory as the weight ring
PDL: weight boxes requested before griddepcontrol.wait, launch_dependents at entry
planned: cluster TMA multicast of the token box (R=384), die-local weight homing + per-die chunks, kind::mxf8f6f4 2x-K with in-kernel activation quant, oversized shared memory
plan: SOL design (19:15) stands for the stream; measured 20:40 that the critical path is the post-dependency chain, so the kernel must minimise work after griddepcontrol.wait:

A. DSMEM cluster split-K (cluster = the K-split contributors of one weight tile, 2 CTAs/SM so clusters of 4-8 co-schedule): partials to own smem, cluster barrier, owners sum peers' partials over DSMEM in rank order, one rounding; replaces the L2 counter protocol (target tail <= 1 us)
B. more CTAs than SMs (grid 2 x SMs measured better) so each SM's post-wait MMA/x work halves; check per-MMA issue time at N=32-128 (stamp 7 'last_full' vs acc_full already in the code)
C. 2-CTA (cta_group::2) M256 for R >= 256 rows (KDA in/o, DSA qkv_a/g/o at r16/r24) to halve x ingest per SM

D. cross-op overlap: issue independent GEMMs (router || latent_down, shared gu on the side stream) as one launch; fuse router into latent_down (same input, one GEMM over the concatenated weight; measured correct)
E. MXFP8 variant (kind::mxf8f6f4 K64 sm_107a, SF 128x4 layout via tcgen05.cp 32x128b.warpx4, fused activation quant) once A-C beat cuBLAS
F. wire into sdec (DecodeProjection kind 'stream'), unit tests, step_d A/B on an int overlay, landed-ready
